name: slower-tempo-more-air
style: late-90s New York street rap, one heavyset MC on a laid-back, relaxed pacing who drags each line a hair behind the snare and lets the last word hang, unbothered talking cadence, lots of breathing room between lines, a deliberate beat of silence right before each punchline lands. Vocal: enormous man, low velvet chest baritone, lazy Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze audible on every inhale, dry and right on the mic. Instrumental: 82 BPM, unhurried swung dusty breakbeat with a thick knocking kick and a hard flat snare, a melancholy after-midnight Rhodes-and-organ soul-jazz figure sliced into a cold, menacing minor loop, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; between the rules a hoarse sampled crowd-chant voice barks the number; bare, minimal, threatening, no hook
exclude: double-time flow, rapid-fire delivery, crammed syllables, sung chorus, female vocals, autotune
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.
[pause]

[Verse 1]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.
[pause]

[Verse 2]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.
[pause]

[Verse 3]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.
[pause]

[Verse 4]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.
[pause]

[Verse 5]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.
[pause]

[Verse 6]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.
[pause]

[Verse 7]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.
[pause]

[Verse 8]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.
[pause]

[Verse 9]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.
[pause]

[Verse 10]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.
[pause]

[Outro]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
